messages:
oliver: Heads-up — sec-scan-bot flagged a kubeconfig in the CI cache of the private submodule checkout. Found in runner artifact: ci/cache/submodules/payments-service/kubeconfig

sec-scan-bot: automated detection -> pattern 'kubeconfig' matched in artifact s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/runner-6789/checkout.tar.gz. severity: high.

samira: thanks. is this from a recent build? which branch/job?

oliver: job: ci/test-integration (runner-6789). build #4521, triggered 2026-03-16. artifact path shows: checkout/submodules/payments-service/deploy/kubeconfig

jason: if it's an actual kubeconfig with a token we need immediate containment: rotate the k8s serviceaccount token, revoke any IAM/SA keys that referenced that cluster, and delete the artifact from S3. also block the runner id until we confirm no other leaks.

maria: confirm whether it was ever committed to git history or only present in the submodule at runtime? run a git grep across main repos and a gitleaks scan.

oliver: quick grep across main repo returned nothing. looks like the submodule was a private repo that stores a demo kubeconfig in its deploy/ dir — not in our main git history, only in the runner checkout and cached artifact.

jason: steps I'm doing now:
- revoke SA token and create new in cluster 'prod-payments'
- rotate any linked cloud creds (IAM role tokens) used by that SA
- delete artifact from S3 and remove from runner cache

commands:```
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/runner-6789/checkout.tar.gz --profile ci-ops
kubectl -n infra delete secret runner-legacy-sa-token-abc123
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete key-id --iam-account=ci-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

sec-oncall: filed INC-842 for the leak (assigned to eng-security). Created timeline entry and set priority P2. Notifying legal and customer support to prep comms if we find external exposure.

samira: please also run a targeted scan across our artifact bucket for other kubeconfig/yaml files. use this helper to list recent artifacts:```
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/ --recursive --human-readable --summarize | grep kubeconfig
```

sec-scan-bot: quick audit run -> matched 1 additional artifact referencing 'apiVersion: v1' in path runner-6710/old-checkout.tar.gz (investigating).

maria: add masking and removal in the pipeline: set KUBECONFIG as a masked env var, remove any step that writes kubeconfigs to workspace, and add a post-job scrub step:```
# scrub artifacts
find $CI_WORKSPACE -type f -name 'kubeconfig' -exec shred -u {} \;
```

jason: post-incident action list (short):
- rotate cluster SA tokens + cloud keys (done by EOD)
- delete artifacts and expire runner caches (in progress)
- add artifact content scan on upload for 'kubeconfig' and block publish
- update CI templates to never checkout private submodules containing secrets by default; require gated fetch
- add alert rule in Splunk/Datadog for any artifact upload with 'apiVersion: v1' or 'kind: Config'

oliver: i'll open PRs to change the pipeline config and add the scrub step. also will contact the submodule owners to remove demo kubeconfigs from repo and add example placeholder files.

samira: good. timeline request: can we have rotation + artifact deletion completed and ticket updated within 4 hours? if not, escalate.

sec-oncall: update: artifact deletion complete, runner blocked, SA token revoked. added notes to INC-842.

maria: once stable, let's plan a retro: update onboarding docs that private submodules must not contain prod credentials, and put CI-side KMS/Vault mounting for any cluster creds.

jason: also will run an org-wide gitleaks + artifact scan for last 90 days and post results to the ticket.

oliver: thanks everyone — I'll keep INC-842 updated.

sec-scan-bot: closing automated alert (ticket INC-842) -> manual review required.
